title.narrative: Scaling up the IMPALA system in Rwanda

description.narrative: Goal 3 B.V. has worked for years on the development of the IMPALA system, a smart data-driven patient monitoring system aimed at hospitals in developing countries. With this system, health professionals can diagnose critical illnesses in newborns faster and better at an early stage. This leads to better quality and more efficient services, a decrease in neonatal mortality and time and cost savings for hospitals. The IMPALA system is made for the African context due to its robustness, ease of use and digital applications.In recent decades, much attention has been paid to improving health care in Rwanda. However, neonatal deaths are still relatively high and there is still little continuous patient monitoring in Rwandan district hospitals. In addition, there are other problems such as major shortages of personnel, lack of suitable medical devices and associated training for personnel.Goal 3 has 2 major potential customers interested in the IMPALA system:• Rwanda Biomedical Center (RBC); the implementing organisation of the Rwandan Ministry of Health (MOH). Because 90% of hospitals in Rwanda are publicly funded, the RBC is the biggest potential customer for Goal 3.• Partners in Health Rwanda (PIH); an American non-governmental organisation (NGO) active in maternal and child care.Both local partners want more information and proof that the system can function properly in the Rwandan context and that the system meets all standards before making a purchasing decision.This study aims to demonstrate, among other things, that the system meets all standards in terms of accuracy and precision of measurements, as well as ease of use.
